items.text: Imported goods should face few or no extra taxes or rules compared with goods made in the country.
items.rationale: Free-trade lean; replaces 'equal terms', which protectionists also claim. Mirrors glo-06.

items.text: Money should be free to move into and out of a country, even when large sudden flows can shake the local economy.
items.rationale: Strong capital mobility with the cost stated; avoids 'no limits' absolute (sanctions). Mirrors glo-07.

items.text: If imports make everyday goods cheaper for most families, they should be allowed in even when some local jobs are lost.
items.rationale: Open-favouring condition (consumer gains); likely frame split. Mirrors glo-08.

items.text: People and organisations from abroad should be able to own businesses in a country on the same terms as locals.
items.rationale: National treatment; 'organisations' keeps it answerable under any ownership regime. Mirrors glo-09.

items.text: If a local industry can survive only with tariffs or other protection from imports, it should be left to shrink or close.
items.note: Tariff: a tax charged on goods brought in from another country.
items.rationale: Open-favouring condition (sheltered industry); strong because it accepts closure. Mirrors glo-10.

items.text: Goods made in the country should have an advantage over imports, for example through tariffs or rules favouring local products.
items.note: Tariff: a tax charged on goods brought in from another country.
items.rationale: Mainstream protectionism; 'rules' excludes voluntary buy-local campaigns. Mirrors glo-01.

items.text: Money moving into and out of a country should be tightly controlled, even if this makes outside investment harder to attract.
items.rationale: Strong capital controls with the cost stated, matching glo-02's structure.

items.text: If cheap imports are forcing a local industry to close, it should be shielded from them.
items.rationale: Protected-favouring condition (industry loss); likely frame split. Mirrors glo-03.

items.text: Major companies in a country should be owned mainly by people or organisations based there.
items.rationale: Local ownership, neutral on private vs public owners. Mirrors glo-04.

items.text: If a crisis abroad cuts off a country's medicine supply, it should make its own from then on, even at much higher cost.
items.rationale: Supply-chain self-reliance; real (not ever-true) condition, single good, strong via lasting high cost. Mirrors glo-05.
